transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on whether the issue is just a broken drive belt. If so, replacing the belt is usually an affordable repair for a nine-year-old machine. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drive belt [belt-driven machines ONLY]. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
I've turned it by hand with the power off and it turns freely and quietly, no scraping or rumbling. It doesn't feel stiff at all.
Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?

I haven't run a spin-only programme as such, but in the normal wash cycle the drum never turns at all, and it doesn't spin at the end either. So I'd expect an empty spin to be the same. Shall I try it anyway?

Yes, you should run a spin-only or rinse and spin programme to see if the drum spins up properly. This test will help determine if the issue is specific to certain cycles or affects all spinning operations. Run a spin-only (or rinse and spin) programme with the washing in. Does the drum spin up properly on that programme?

Ok, I'll try a rinse and spin programme with the drum empty, as I said I'd expect the same result. I'll let you know, but it's not turning at all in the normal wash, so I doubt it will spin. By the way, I did once notice a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, though not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
